question.problem:
Given the function $f(x;w)={w}_{1}{x}_{1}+{w}_{2}{x}_{2},$ compute ${∇}_{w}\,f$ with the input $x={[\begin{aligned}5,\,3\end{aligned}]}^{T}.$
${∇}_{w}\,f=\text{ }$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
To compute ${∇}_{w}\,f$, we take partial derivatives with respect to each component of $w.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{w}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{w}_{1}}({w}_{1}{x}_{1}+{w}_{2}{x}_{2})={x}_{1} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{w}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{w}_{2}}({w}_{1}{x}_{1}+{w}_{2}{x}_{2})={x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, with $x={[\begin{aligned}5,\,3\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{w}\,f & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
